An authorized warehouse worker can open the staff shipment screen, scan the device signed QR, see the resolved device + active ASSIGNED assignment + linked channel order (or pick among candidates), upload a label photo, confirm the OCR draft, and submit; the same success/failure/retry semantics as admin apply.

assertions.statement: The admin shipment panel and the staff shipment screen render loading, empty (no assignable device / no active assignment), permission-denied, write-disabled, shop-not-authorized, OCR-failed, scan-rejected (staff only), and ship-failed states.
assertions.evidence_ref: sensory:report.json/report.md review of existing browser screenshots, UI states, negative-path unit/runtime evidence, and staff submit screenshots

assertions.statement: POST /admin-api/rental/xianyu/order/ship refuses with XIANYU_WRITE_DISABLED when rental.xianyu.write-enabled is false.
POST /admin-api/rental/xianyu/order/ship refuses with the existing XIANYU_SHOP_AUTHORIZATION_INVALID when the target shop is not currently authorized (no new error code is created for this case).

A ship call uses self-developed-app MD5 signing with canonical UTF-8 JSON bytes via a NEW XianyuWriteClient (NOT XianyuReadClient); the read-only XianyuReadClient/XianyuReadEndpoint allowlist is not modified.
The local assignment advances ASSIGNED->DISPATCHED and a rental_device_shipment row is persisted only after XianGuanJia ship returns success; on failure neither is persisted.
Repeating a ship call with the same idempotency key returns the first successful result and does not call XianGuanJia again; repeating with a different key on the same assignment is rejected.
The ship endpoint only accepts an assignment that is ASSIGNED and tenant-scoped to the operator; any other state is rejected with no XianGuanJia call.
Duplicate waybills for the same channel order are rejected by a unique constraint on (tenant_id, channel_order_id, waybill_no, express_code).

Both admin and staff ship calls hit the same /rental/xianyu/order/ship endpoint; the request carries a source value (ADMIN/STAFF) recorded on the shipment row; the backend does not branch business rules on source.

rental_device_shipment follows RentalDeviceAssignmentDO conventions: extends TenantBaseDO, @TableName/@TableId/@KeySequence, mapper extends BaseMapperX, soft-delete via inherited deleted bit. Stores channel order id, assignment id, waybill, express code/name, request body hash, response code/msg, OCR-confirmed flag, source (admin/staff), tenant, timestamps; waybill masked in non-detail kanban/export.

The OCR config yudao.ai.mimo base-url/api-key/model/enable is read from config only; the api-key never appears in a log, frontend payload, or fixture; OCR failure degrades to an empty draft and never blocks manual entry.
assertions.evidence_ref: static:ShipmentOcrProperties prefix yudao.ai.shipment-ocr + application.yaml NEWAPI fallback + OCR fallback tests; requirements text updated after user clarified not mimo

Production must set RENTAL_DEVICE_QR_SECRET to enforce signed QRs; unsigned local fallback is existing behavior, not a new risk.
